title: Leadership in Israel: Saul
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The learner discusses reasons for kingship in Israel (Samuel old, his sons corrupt, wish to be like the nations, a leader for war; 1 Samuel 8:1-5, 19-20) and reasons against it (God was their king, a king would take their sons, land and harvest; 1 Samuel 8:7, 11-18).

floor.question: Name one leadership quality of Moses.

representations: two columns: for and against kingship
a list of what a king would take

board.do: Draw two columns: for kingship and against.

board.say: What did God say the people were rejecting?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say God as king.

misconceptions.ask: Why did Israel ask for a king?
misconceptions.repair: Read 1 Samuel 8:1-5: Samuel was old; his sons took bribes; the people wanted a king like the nations.

misconceptions.ask: What did Samuel warn a king would do?
misconceptions.repair: Read 1 Samuel 8:11-18 and list what a king would take: sons, daughters, fields, a tenth.

listen_for: To be different from all other nations
misconceptions.ask: What did Israel want, according to 1 Samuel 8:20?
misconceptions.repair: Read 1 Samuel 8:5 and 8:20: they wanted to be like other nations, with a king to lead and fight.

misconceptions.ask: What did God tell Samuel the people were really rejecting (1 Samuel 8:7)?
misconceptions.repair: Read 1 Samuel 8:7 and discuss why God, not Samuel, was rejected.

checks.question: Why did Israel ask for a king?
checks.answer: Samuel was old and his sons did not follow his ways

checks.question: What did Samuel warn a king would do?
checks.answer: Take their sons, land and harvest

skills.key_step: The learner evaluates Saul's failures (offering the sacrifice at Gilgal without waiting, sparing the best of the Amalekites, excuses and blaming the people, seeking a medium) and their consequences (God rejected him as king; 1 Samuel 13:13-14; 15:22-23), and deduces lessons for leaders (obey God fully, be patient, own mistakes).

floor.prerequisite: Knows why Israel asked for a king.
floor.question: Why did Israel want a king?

representations: a time line of Saul's reign

board.do: Write 1 Samuel 15:22: "To obey is better than sacrifice".

board.say: What did Saul do wrong here?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say he spared the best against God's command.

misconceptions.ask: What did Saul do at Gilgal?
misconceptions.repair: Read 1 Samuel 13:8-13: Saul did not wait and offered the burnt offering himself.

misconceptions.ask: What did Saul do with the best Amalekite flocks?
misconceptions.repair: Read 1 Samuel 15:9, 22: "To obey is better than sacrifice". Partial obedience is disobedience.

misconceptions.ask: What was the result of Saul's disobedience?
misconceptions.repair: Read 1 Samuel 15:23, 26: God rejected Saul as king; David was anointed (1 Samuel 16).

misconceptions.ask: What did Samuel tell Saul in 1 Samuel 15:22?
misconceptions.repair: Read 1 Samuel 15:22 and ask: can a gift replace doing what God said?

checks.question: What did Saul do at Gilgal?
checks.answer: Offered the sacrifice himself instead of waiting for Samuel
